title: 025 · Why? #13: Galton board, fair pegs but the middle wins (70 of 256 paths; predict-first, white)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Probability. 256 balls, 8 rows of pegs. Which bin fills most? A middle · B edges · C all equal 👇

A. Every peg is a fair 50–50, yet the middle wins.
Why? There are 256 left/right paths, each equally likely. Only 1 reaches an edge bin (all lefts). 70 reach the middle.
The paths per bin are Pascal's triangle: 1, 8, 28, 56, 70, 56, 28, 8, 1 = ⁸Cₖ.
Trap: "each peg is fair, so each bin is fair" (C). Fair steps, unfair bins.

Each peg is a coin toss, so NDA asked it in 2018 (II), Q107: 8 coins, at least 6 heads = (28 + 8 + 1)/256 = 37/256.
